story.head: The Sharks need a win
paras: The Sharks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Islanders (7-6-2) lost 5-3 to Carolina on Thursday. Going in, the Islanders are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Sharks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th).

The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd), so the Isles have the edge over the Sharks on depth. The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). San Jose has scored 2.44 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Sharks (3rd), so expect plenty of it.

Matthew Schaefer (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the Islanders in scoring, and Bo Horvat (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 15 GP) has a team-high seven goals. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 16 GP).

Yaroslav Askarov (4-8-0 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for San Jose. the Islanders has two options in net: Ilya Sorokin (6-4-0 / .911 SV% in 10 GS) and Semyon Varlamov (1-2-2 / .891 SV% in 5 GS). Sorokin has started six of their last ten games, but Varlamov got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Islanders are newly without Ryan Pulock, have been without Matias Maccelli since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Mathew Barzal all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Ducks are missing more right now.
The Sharks have been without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg for several games.
With Alexander Wennberg out, Collin Graf took 15 faceoffs in the Sharks’ last game. He had been taking fewer than one a game.
